title: 12 Best Shan Noodles in Mandalay
description: The best Shan noodles in Mandalay — curated from Reddit reviews and travel blogs. Shan Ma Ma, Unique Mandalay, Pan Cherry & more. Interactive map included.

places.name: Shan Ma Ma (ရှမ်းမမ)

redditQuotes.text: Shan Ma Ma is the go-to. Lemon chicken, Shan noodle soups with great spice add ons. Wonderful service.
Shan Ma Ma is a Mandalay institution. You'll see locals and tourists packed in at all hours. The noodles are consistently good and the prices are absurdly cheap.
redditQuotes.source: — travel blog · Restaurants in Mandalay guide

places.verdict: The most-reviewed Shan noodle shop in Mandalay for a reason.

Not the most authentic hidden gem, but the one you can always count on.

The classic dry Shan noodles (shan khaut swè) with chicken or pork are a must. Get the broth on the side for dipping and add their house chili oil for extra kick. Their lemon chicken and Shan tofu are also excellent choices.

places.name: Unique Mandalay Tea Room

redditQuotes.text: A warm, delicious, and flavorful Shan noodle is a true Mandalay favorite. Try Unique Mandalay Tea Room whenever you're in Mandalay.
In our Mandalay, Shan noodles are eaten morning, noon, and night. At Unique Mandalay you can get chicken, pork, pork ribs, and beef balls — mix and match as you like.

places.verdict: The highest-rated noodle spot in Mandalay on TripAdvisor (4.7★, 239 reviews).

A proper Mandalay morning experience.

places.name: Pan Cherry Noodle House & Café (ပန်ချယ်ရီ)

redditQuotes.text: Pan Cherry Noodle House has stood the test of time, recently celebrating its 40th anniversary. The humble shop belies the intricate flavors and textures of their signature Shan noodles.
redditQuotes.source: — Myanmore · Serving Mandalay's best noodles since 1978

redditQuotes.text: Countless tourists have made Pan Cherry a daily pit stop on their Mandalay itinerary — they come once for a meal and find themselves returning the next day and the next!

comparison.best for: Noodle House in 25th St, Chanayethazan with a 1,500–4,000 MMK spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.3★ from 246 Google reviews · Noodle House · 25th St, Chanayethazan
comparison.why it made the list: The heritage pick. Pan Cherry has been serving Shan noodles since 1978, founded by a Shan State native who brought his recipe straight from Kyauk Me. Now run by the second generation, the consistency is remarkable — regulars have been coming every morning for decades. The two-story building with an air-con café upstairs is a nice touch when Mandalay's heat hits.

The signature Shan noodles are a must-try — the recipe hasn't changed since the founder brought it from Kyauk Me in Shan State in 1978. Their stir-fried noodles and dumplings are also worth trying.

places.name: Mogok Daw Shan Noodle (မိုးကုတ်တော်)

redditQuotes.text: I recommend the Shan noodle with meatball, dry. The noodle is so fresh with egg smell, every bite you can feel the juice from it, this is one of the best meals we had in Myanmar.

Good street corner restaurant in Mandalay. It's very cheap and the food is tasty. It's an open air restaurant with mostly local people there. We had a tea leaves salad, a crispy pork noodle soup and dumplings. Everything was very good.

comparison.strengths: 3.9★ from 298 Google reviews · Shan Noodle Shop · 33rd St, Chanayethazan
comparison.why it made the list: The local's local. Mogok Daw is pure street-level Mandalay — open air, plastic stools, a mostly-Burmese crowd, and noodles that cost pocket change. The hand-pulled dumplings made right in front of you are worth the visit alone. English menu with pictures makes ordering easy despite the language barrier.

The Shan noodle with meatball (dry style) is highly recommended — the fresh egg noodles are exceptional. Also try the crispy pork noodle soup, dumplings (freshly made by four people out front), and the tea leaf salad.

places.name: 999 Shan Noodle Shop (၉၉၉ ရှမ်းခေါက်ဆွဲ)

redditQuotes.text: Arguably the best Shan noodles outside of Shan State. Traditional Burmese noodle recipe — fresh daily-made noodles served in a range of soups and sauces at very affordable prices.
The Shan Noodle with Oil was so tasty. The noodles had the smooth chewy texture reminiscent of Chinese hand-pulled noodles. The pork and 'oil' toppings were just right.

places.verdict: Featured in Lonely Planet and a perennial favorite among backpackers.

places.verdict: The buffet approach lets you sample a wide range of Shan dishes in one sitting — perfect for first-timers who want to taste everything.

places.name: Golden Shan / Shwe Shan (ရွှေရှမ်း)

redditQuotes.text: We went to Shwe Shan for buffet because I was really hungry. It feels like eating chap chye peng — you pick your own favorite dishes. I had more than 10 dishes on my plate. The buffet is only 4000 kyat and the standard of the food is very good!
redditQuotes.source: — Miss Tam Chiak · 10 Must-Try Mandalay Street Food

redditQuotes.text: The lady spoke fantastic English and was very helpful in introducing the dishes! Many of them have Chinese influence and have flavourful taste profile.
redditQuotes.source: — Miss Tam Chiak · Mandalay food guide

comparison.best for: Shan Buffet in 84th St, between 22nd & 23rd St with a 3,000–5,000 MMK spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.2★ from 210 Google reviews · Shan Buffet · 84th St, between 22nd & 23rd St
comparison.why it made the list: The best bang-for-your-kyat in Mandalay. 4,000 MMK (~$2 USD) for a heaping plate of 10+ dishes is almost comically cheap. The Chinese-Shan fusion flavors are distinctive — this isn't just rice and curry. The English-speaking staff are a bonus for tourists navigating an unfamiliar buffet line.

Pick your own dishes from the buffet spread — aim for 5–10 dishes on your plate. The Chinese-influenced preparations are the standout. Shan noodles are always available alongside the curries and stir-fries.

places.name: Shwe Muse Shan Noodle (ရွှေမူဆယ်)

redditQuotes.text: Best noodles I've ever taken. Authentic Shan flavour.
Shwe Muse Shan Noodle is a popular spot in Mandalay known for its authentic Shan cuisine. The restaurant offers a variety of traditional dishes with strong and interesting flavours.

comparison.why it made the list: The authenticity pick. Shwe Muse doesn't cater to tourists — this is where Mandalay locals go for a straightforward, no-frills bowl of Shan noodles with properly bold flavors. If you want to taste Shan noodles the way they're meant to taste — not toned down for foreign palates — this is your spot.

redditQuotes.text: Teashop Karaweik does excellent Shan noodles and sweet naan straight from the tandoor, best enjoyed alongside a cup of tea.

places.verdict: The Fodor's pick, and for good reason.

comparison.best for: Tea Shop / Noodles in Near 84th & 23rd St area with a 1,500–3,000 MMK spend range

comparison.why it made the list: The Fodor's pick, and for good reason. The combination of Shan noodles and fresh tandoor naan reflects Mandalay's unique position at the crossroads of Shan, Burmese, and Indian food cultures. It's a tea shop first — meaning the vibe is pure local morning energy. Come early.

places.name: Shwe Pyi Moe Tea Shop (ရွှေပြည်မိုး)

redditQuotes.text: Shwe Pyi Moe Tea Shop, a very famous breakfast stop for all Burmese. Shan noodles are served everywhere, at all hours of the day, and it is equally filling but more tangy. The toss of peanuts, fresh cilantro, onion and preserved vegetables makes it light enough to keep me full and happy, yet craving for more.
redditQuotes.source: — Miss Tam Chiak · Must-Try Mandalay Street Food

comparison.best for: Tea Shop / Breakfast in 66th St, between 26th & 27th St with a 1,000–2,500 MMK spend range

comparison.why it made the list: The breakfast champion. Every Mandalay morning starts at a tea shop, and Shwe Pyi Moe next to Sedona Hotel is where the locals go. Their Shan noodles lean tangy and light — Thai-influenced with the sweet-sour-salty balance — making them ideal first thing in the morning. Opens at 5 AM for the early risers.

Both are served alongside sweet Burmese tea.

places.name: 16th Street Myee Shay

redditQuotes.text: This no-name stall along Street 16 sells excellent Myee Shay which draws a huge crowd. For only US$1, you get a bowl of rice noodles full of ingredients including pig's tail and pig's skin, plus a super flavourful bowl of pork ribs soup.
redditQuotes.source: — Miss Tam Chiak · Must-Try Mandalay Street Food

redditQuotes.text: Mandalay myi shay — the rice noodles are served with chicken or pork and topped with a generous blob of sticky glutinous rice 'glue'. It was slimy and did not look appealing initially, but once mixed in with the rest of the noodles, it actually tasted pretty good.
redditQuotes.source: — Life After 9 to 5 · Eating in Mandalay

comparison.why it made the list: The street stall experience. This nameless stall is the real deal — roadside plastic stools, zero English, and a huge local crowd that tells you everything you need to know. Meeshay is Mandalay's own spin on Shan noodles and this is where to try it. The slimy rice topping is an acquired texture, but the flavor is undeniable. Opens 8:30 AM, closes by 3 PM — come at lunch.

places.name: Marie Min

redditQuotes.text: Burmese, Indian, and western dishes pack the vegetarian menu at this Sri Lankan family place. Most come here for lunch and dinner, snagging coveted seats on the upper-level balcony.
Tea Leaf Salad at Marie Min Vegetarian Restaurant — totally unique and utterly delicious.
redditQuotes.source: — Gallop Around the Globe · Cuisine of Myanmar

comparison.best for: Vegetarian-Friendly in 27th St, between 74th & 75th St with a 2,000–5,000 MMK spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.2★ from 229 Google reviews · Vegetarian-Friendly · 27th St, between 74th & 75th St
comparison.why it made the list: The vegetarian-friendly pick. If you're traveling meat-free in Myanmar (not easy), Marie Min is your lifeline. With 592 TripAdvisor reviews and a faithful backpacker following, it's the rare Mandalay restaurant where vegetarian Shan noodles are done with real care — not just the meat version minus the meat. The balcony seating is a nice bonus.
